title: A new sense of purpose
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What would you chase if money were out of the way?

A student said the person in the book finds a new sense of purpose in this chapter. Jose said he has friends who made a ton of money and then their sense of purpose changed, not in a negative way. They have a little more luxury, because the money is out of the way.

They no longer have to compromise with their purpose or the way they do things, he said. If you put yourself in their shoes, you can now entertain a higher purpose, because you are at that stage of your life.

A student said: it's also looking for a much larger problem to solve. Once you accomplish the money piece, it never really goes away, but you still need something bigger to chase to get you up every day.
Jose said one phrase from the chapter was etched into his brain, and he would put it on a wall.
unwavering certainty in the face of challenge.
That is what he is, Jose said: absolutely unwavering. When we look at the people around us, who gives us that sense of motivation, focus and ambition, and that kind of relentless discovery?
What bigger problem would get you up every day?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write what you would work on if money were out of the way.
Write the larger problem it would solve.
Write what keeps you certain when you face a challenge.
Write who around you gives you that certainty.
Write where you compromise your purpose today.

check.q: What did a student say people look for once the money is accomplished?
choices: A much larger problem to solve

check.q: What phrase did Jose say he would put on a wall?
choices: Unwavering certainty in the face of challenge

check.q: What does Jose say changes for people who made a lot of money?

recap: Look for the larger problem. Hold your certainty when things get hard.
